title: Forest fire: questions and safety instructions for callers
approval_status: DEMO CONTENT - not approved by a fire service. Based on the public advice listed in sources.

sources.title: SRF Ratgeber: Fünf Regeln - Wie verhalte ich mich bei einem Waldbrand?
sources.note: Advice quoted from Alberto Ceronetti (deputy commander, Feuerwehr Mendrisiotto), AlertSwiss and BAFU; translated to English.

recognition: Smoke, flames or strong heat are clear warning signs, even when there is no official warning yet.
questions: Where exactly do you see the fire or the smoke? Name a landmark, path, road or railway line.
How big is the fire? Is it near houses, a road, a railway line or on a slope?
Which way does the smoke move?
Are you or other people in danger now? How many people are with you?
instructions: If you see smoke or flames or feel strong heat, leave the area at once.
Never flee uphill: fire spreads faster uphill. Move downhill or along the slope, away from the fire.
Avoid narrow valleys and gullies. A stream does not give reliable protection.
An area that has already burned is safer, because material burns only once.
If you are already in a car, it is usually safer to stay in it than to go out into the heat and smoke.
Follow the instructions of the authorities (AlertSwiss, police, fire brigade). Return only when the authorities allow it.
